rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable aphthous ulcer (mouth symptoms page)
rule_level_problems.problem: Evidence is the bare 'Ulcer of mouth' (disorder), so every mouth ulcer and every descendant (traumatic, drug-induced, thermal/chemical burn ulceration, recurrent ulcer) yields a probable aphthous ulcer. The page's discriminators 'painful' and 'with central white patch' are lost. This is the one probable rule on the page whose trigger is materially broader than the page.

The approach box says 'If on abacavir, check for abacavir hypersensitivity reaction (AHR) 131'. By the house standard this is a 'consider X' and should be a possible rule triggered by mouth symptoms plus abacavir exposure, the same pre-screen pattern used for anaphylaxis in this file. 'Abacavir' (substance) and 'Hypersensitivity to abacavir' / 'Allergy to abacavir' (finding) exist in SNOMED; whether a finding-category concept is accepted as a diagnosis would need confirming. No rule or check_for item exists for it.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable angular cheilitis / impetigo around the mouth / contact dermatitis at corners of mouth
rule_level_problems.problem: All three share the fissure trigger with no exclusions, so a patient with cracked corners plus perioral crusts and blisters receives probable angular cheilitis AND probable impetigo, and one with severe itching receives probable angular cheilitis AND probable contact dermatitis. The page frames impetigo and contact dermatitis as alternative conclusions ('If crusts and blisters ... impetigo likely', 'If very itchy, contact dermatitis likely'). The language has (not ...) to express the exclusion. Reasonable people could leave this as is.

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded: Unable to open mouth and the sudden face/tongue swelling AND any-of-ten-signs criterion both reach an Urgent priority rule with the page's and/or structure, the allergen footnote is expanded to drug, food and insect bite/sting, and 'check for anaphylaxis' is a possible pre-screen rule; every SNOMED concept in the file resolves. The most consequential problem is the aphthous ulcer rule, which fires on any mouth ulcer or descendant because 'painful' and 'central white patch' were dropped. Second is a missing possible rule for 'If on abacavir, check for abacavir hypersensitivity reaction', which the house standard treats as a 'consider X'; the remaining gaps (redness dropped from the examination list and the angular cheilitis trigger, 'painful' dropped from the blister trigger, the three corner-of-mouth rules co-firing) are low severity.
